title: Analyst, Procurement Contracts
description:
About Arevon

Arevon is a U.S. energy leader committed to powering America with affordable, reliable, and secure homegrown energy. Headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona, and with a regional office in New York City, the company’s experienced and dedicated team develops, finances, builds, owns, and operates renewable energy projects nationwide. With a strong track record in utility-scale solar and energy storage, Arevon is a trusted partner to utilities and businesses seeking cost-effective, sustainable energy solutions. By prioritizing American manufacturing and domestic energy production, the company invests in U.S. jobs, strengthens local economies, and advances the country’s energy independence.

The Position

Arevon is recruiting for the position of Analyst, Contracts Management. This role is intended for a highly organized, detail-oriented professional who is ready to build foundational commercial contracting skills in a fast-paced renewable energy environment. The successful candidate will support the full contract lifecycle by assisting with drafting, redlining, organizing, version control, stakeholder follow-up, approvals, execution support, and post-execution documentation under the guidance of a Manager or Senior Manager, Contracts Management.

Key Responsibilities

The Analyst, Contracts Management is a supporting member of Arevon’s Contracts Management Department responsible for assisting with commercial contracting matters across utility-scale solar and energy storage projects. This role requires disciplined follow-through, strong organization, attention to detail, and the ability to support time-sensitive contracting work from intake through execution. The Analyst will assist with contract lifecycle activities, including intake, scoping, drafting, redline control, stakeholder follow-up, approvals, execution, and post-execution documentation, while coordinating with Legal, Finance, Engineering, Procurement, Project Management, Construction, Tax, Risk, Insurance, Asset Management, and external counterparties as directed. Additionally, the Analyst, Contracts Management will be responsible for:

Contract Drafting, Execution Support & Workstream Coordination:

  • Support commercial contracting activities for agreements related to the development, construction, and operation of PV and energy storage projects, including EPC agreements, O&M agreements, equipment supply agreements, master terms, amendments, change orders, and related commercial instruments.
  • Assist with negotiation preparation for assigned matters, including issue tracking, redline summaries, fallback position documentation, approval status, risk notes, and recommendations for Manager or Senior Manager review.
  • Draft, redline, compare, and reconcile routine contract documents and comments with accuracy, translating business, technical, financial, insurance, risk, tax, and project delivery inputs into clear contract revisions under appropriate guidance.
  • Coordinate stakeholder inputs and approval follow-up by working across Legal, Finance, Engineering, Procurement, Project Management, Construction, Tax, Risk, Insurance, Development, Asset Management, and other stakeholders as directed.
  • Help drive assigned agreements forward by organizing inputs, chasing outstanding comments, reconciling stakeholder feedback, maintaining status trackers, and supporting timely completion of open items.
  • Support updates to contract templates, forms, checklists, trackers, and approval tools that improve consistency, speed, governance, and auditability across assigned Contracts Management workstreams.

Contract Governance, Redline Oversight & Document Management:

  • Apply and reinforce disciplined redline, version control, approval, and document retention practices across assigned contracts and workstreams.
  • Maintain and review contract records for agreements, amendments, warranties, insurance certificates, notices, deliverables, and related documentation to support a complete, accurate, and auditable contract history.
  • Review counterparty redlines and internal comments, identify apparent negotiation issues and alignment gaps, and escalate business risk, legal risk, technical risk, schedule risk, financing risk, tax risk, and insurance risk for guidance as appropriate.
  • Maintain disciplined redline control and agreement hygiene, including clean comparisons, issue lists, decision logs, signature readiness, approval evidence, and post-execution obligation tracking.
  • Support department standards for traceability, contract administration, knowledge management, and single-source-of-truth documentation.

Stakeholder Coordination & Communication:

  • Serve as a supporting commercial contracts contact for assigned matters with internal stakeholders and external counterparties as directed, helping facilitate document exchange, follow-up, issue tracking, and efficient negotiation support.
  • Prepare concise summaries for internal stakeholders and Contracts Management leadership regarding contract status, open issues, approval needs, and risk items requiring review.
  • Resolve routine process, documentation, and follow-up items where appropriate, and escalate substantive contract or commercial issues with clear context, options, and requested guidance.
  • Capture lessons learned from projects, counterparties, and internal business partners and help translate those lessons into improved contract language, trackers, checklists, and department procedures.
  • Support financing, diligence, and contract review requests by preparing accurate summaries of key terms, obligations, risk mitigants, and deal protections for leadership review.

Department Operations, Process Support & Continuous Improvement:

  • Support department initiatives to improve contract lifecycle management, reporting, compliance tracking, approvals, handoffs, and post-execution administration.
  • Support contracting workflows, SOPs, checklists, metrics, and controls for assigned areas that promote quality, accountability, auditability, and on-time execution.
  • Share knowledge and lessons learned with team members to support consistent drafting quality, risk assessment, negotiation preparation, and process discipline.
  • Support assigned post-execution contract priorities, including key obligations, renewals, expirations, notices, change management, closeout requirements, and lessons learned, escalating material issues as appropriate.

Required Qualifications

  • 0–2 years of contracts management experience, including experience or demonstrated interest in contract drafting, redlining, contract administration, document control, approval routing, procurement contracting, or related commercial support.
  • 0–1 year of renewable energy experience preferred but not required, particularly experience or exposure supporting utility-scale solar, battery energy storage, construction, procurement, EPC, O&M, equipment supply, or related commercial contracting matters.
  • Hands-on experience supporting contract matters beyond document routing, including drafting, redlining, organizing, reconciling comments, chasing inputs, maintaining trackers, and helping drive agreements toward execution.
  • Ability to describe how prior work, coursework, internship experience, or related administrative support helped support commercial outcomes, stakeholder alignment, accurate documentation, or timely completion of assigned matters.
  • Interest in EPC contracting, project delivery models, and how commercial terms impact construction execution, change management, schedule certainty, cost exposure, performance obligations, warranty recovery, financing diligence, and project closeout outcomes.
  • Strong analytical and organizational skills, with the ability to help translate project, counterparty, and stakeholder needs into practical contracting tools, including templates, trackers, approval checklists, issue logs, and decision records.
  • Strong communication and follow-through skills; able to build rapport, manage open items, coordinate competing inputs, and support internal stakeholders, contractors, suppliers, and external counterparties in reaching timely agreements.
  • Proficiency in contract drafting, redlining, version control, document comparison, and maintaining a clear decision record through Microsoft Word and related contract management tools.
  • Ability to review and support revisions to contract language with attention to nuance, intent, risk allocation, operational impacts, and business implications, escalating questions when appropriate.
  • Collaborative, outcomes-focused professional able to support cross-functional stakeholders, track assigned decisions, and deliver results with guidance from a Manager or Senior Manager.
  • Experience supporting or improving contracting processes, templates, playbooks, SOPs, reporting practices, or compliance controls that improve consistency, auditability, speed, and quality across commercial contract workstreams.
  • AI curiosity and eagerness to leverage AI-enabled tools to improve contracting efficiency, drafting quality, redline review, knowledge management, reporting, and legal or commercial workflow discipline.
  • Self-starter with sound judgment, humility, urgency, attention to detail, and follow-through; able to prioritize competing tasks, communicate status clearly, and escalate issues with context and a recommended next step.
  • Demonstrated commitment to fostering diverse, equitable, and inclusive collaboration across internal stakeholders, external counterparties, and project partners.
  • Working knowledge of procurement and contracting organizations, including supplier engagement, contract records, cross-functional approvals, and the role of contracting in broader business execution.
  • Proficient with Microsoft Office Suite and contract management, reporting, or visualization tools; experience with Power BI, CLM platforms, document control systems, or AI-enabled workflow tools is a plus. Ability and willingness to travel as needed and work occasional overtime on short notice to support critical negotiations, closings, or project milestones.

title: Manager, Business Systems
description:
About Arevon

Arevon is a U.S. energy leader committed to powering America with affordable, reliable, and secure homegrown energy. Headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona, and with a regional office in New York City, the company’s experienced and dedicated team develops, finances, builds, owns, and operates renewable energy projects nationwide. With a strong track record in utility-scale solar and energy storage, Arevon is a trusted partner to utilities and businesses seeking cost-effective, sustainable energy solutions. By prioritizing American manufacturing and domestic energy production, the company invests in U.S. jobs, strengthens local economies, and advances the country’s energy independence.

The Position

Arevon is recruiting for the position of Manager, Business Systems, an outstanding opportunity for an experienced systems leader to run NetSuite and Sitetracker, two platforms the whole company relies on, in one of the most important industries for the 21st century.

Your time divides evenly between the two. On the NetSuite side, you will administer the system to support the needs of the business, working closely with Accounting, Finance, and the teams who rely on it. Sitetracker, Arevon’s Salesforce-based platform, is where the company acquires land, signs agreements, procures equipment, builds projects, and keeps them running. You will administer both as part of a team of NetSuite and Sitetracker administrators who share the work, review each other’s changes, and back each other up.

On the Sitetracker side, we build differently from most Salesforce teams. The team directs AI coding agents that write the metadata, Apex, and flows, deploy them to a sandbox, run the tests, and open the pull request, all inside a playbook the team has written and sharpened over hundreds of changes. Every change moves through GitHub with automated validation, an independent QA sign-off, and a weekly release to production, and colleagues can put questions to an AI assistant we built into Sitetracker itself.

As Manager, you bring the judgment that makes all of this work: deciding what gets built and why, setting priorities with the business, and holding every change to the same standard whether a person or an agent wrote it.

This role suits a business systems professional with five or more years of experience who has administered both NetSuite and Salesforce and who enjoys leading as much as building. The Manager reports to the Director, Business Systems (Salesforce). The role is based in Scottsdale, Arizona, with a minimum of three days a week in the office and minimal travel.

Key Responsibilities

NetSuite Administration (50%)

  • Administer NetSuite day to day: users, roles and permissions, custom records and fields, forms, and workflows.
  • Partner with Accounting, Finance, and other business teams to gather requirements and turn them into configuration, workflows, and reports that meet the needs of the business.
  • Build and maintain saved searches, reports, and dashboards that give colleagues timely, accurate information.
  • Maintain role-based access and segregation of duties in support of internal controls and audit requests.
  • Plan and test NetSuite’s twice-yearly releases and keep customizations, scripts, and SuiteApps documented and supportable.
  • Support SuiteScript, SuiteFlow, and integration work, whether built in-house or by a partner.
  • Maintain data integrity across imports, integrations, and master data.

Sitetracker Administration (50%)

  • Administer Sitetracker end to end: users, permission sets, security, and the objects, flows, and record pages colleagues rely on every day.
  • Lead changes through the team’s AI-assisted build workflow: direct AI coding agents such as Claude Code, review the approach they propose, and inspect what they produce before it reaches an org.
  • Carry changes through the path to production: source control in GitHub, automated validation, independent QA, and a weekly release.
  • Turn lessons learned into rules the agents follow automatically, helping maintain the shared playbook, skills, and guardrails that keep the approach safe.
  • Help grow the AI assistant built into Sitetracker, from reviewing the answers it gives colleagues to shaping what it can do next.

Leadership and Collaboration Across Both Platforms

  • Work as one team with Arevon’s NetSuite and Sitetracker administrators: share the load, review each other’s work, cross-train, and cover for one another so neither platform depends on a single person.
  • Set priorities with business leaders in Accounting, Finance, Legal, Project Development, Construction, and Operations, turning requests into clear requirements with acceptance criteria and explaining what is changing and why.
  • Support and train users on both platforms, troubleshooting issues and resolving them promptly.
  • Mentor administrators and analysts and build the documentation, test scripts, and checklists that make the team faster and more consistent.
  • Measure adoption and value: define and report KPIs that show how each platform is used and where it saves time.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Accounting, Finance, Computer Science, Business Administration, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).
  • Five or more years of business systems experience, including at least three years administering NetSuite and at least three years administering Salesforce.
  • Deep NetSuite administration skills: roles and permissions, saved searches, SuiteFlow workflows, custom records and fields, CSV imports, and release testing.
  • Strong Salesforce administration skills: the security model, Flow, and data management, with enough Apex and SOQL to review what others build.

  • Always maintain integrity and follow Arevon safety policies and procedures.
  • Perform varying corrective, preventive, and emergency maintenance for solar PV systems.

  • Ability to perform testing, switching and troubleshooting of low, medium, and high voltage equipment, including transformers, breakers, relays, contactors, motors, trackers, DC array and inverters to name a few.
  • Capable of retrieving relay files and submitting to engineering for review.
  • Assist with writing and enforcing work and equipment testing instructions and procedures, including normal and maintenance operating procedures.
  • Ensure CMMS work orders are complete in their entirety. Prepare documents necessary for procurement and utilization of materials and vendor services.
  • Perform testing using IV Curve Tracers, Power Quality Meters, Insulation Resistance Testers, Multimeters, and other equipment, as needed.
  • Keep track of quality, quantity, and stock levels of all materials on the sites.
  • Proven computer skills in a Windows environment (Microsoft Office Products) are required.
  • Ability to prioritize multiple tasks and projects.
  • Self-directed and accountable, able to think critically about processes and issues.
  • Communicate cross-functionally across all necessary parts of the organization to achieve resolution to plant issues.
  • Maintain work area and site housecleaning to company standards.

  • May be required to support job responsibilities as needed outside of scheduled work hours.
  • Occasional travel may be required.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications

  • 3 years of direct experience as a PV solar technician or 6 years' experience in a non-solar electrical maintenance role.
  • Excellent writing and verbal skills.
  • Valid U.S. Driver license with acceptable MVR history.
  • Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills.
  • Strong communications and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with both technical and non-technical co-workers and vendors.
  • Ability to wear personal protective equipment is required (including but not limited to; steel/composite toed shoes, gloves, safety glasses, hearing protection, protective jacket or apron and arm guards).
  • Will sit, stand, or walk short distances for up to the entire duration of a shift.
  • Will lift, push, or pull up to 50 pounds on an occasional basis.
  • Must be able to comply with all safety standards and procedures.
  • Willingness to work flexible hours and be on-call for emergencies.

Preferred Qualifications

  • CEC license or technical degree preferred. Electrical certifications, state, journeyman, etc. a plus.
  • Experience in operating and maintaining power plant electrical systems, SCADA and controls systems operation, troubleshooting advanced electrical components, and using procedures to perform equipment preventative and corrective maintenance preferred.
